ambiguities.description: The credit value range '1 and 6' is qualified with 'usually', suggesting it may not be a strict/hard constraint but rather a typical range; unclear if values outside this range are disallowed or just uncommon.

source_references.excerpt: The credit value is a whole number, usually between 1 and 6.

ambiguities.description: It's unclear whether grade uniqueness ('at most one grade per offering') means the student may have zero or one grade (optional) rather than exactly one; the mandatory status of the grade role for enrolled students is not explicitly confirmed, especially given the phrase 'at most one' implies grade could be absent even after enrollment (e.g., if course not yet completed, or student withdrew).

source_references.excerpt: A student gets at most one grade per offering.

ambiguities.description: The transcript states a student receives a grade 'for each course offering they were enrolled in', implying every enrollment eventually gets a grade, but combined with 'at most one grade per offering' this creates ambiguity about whether the grade fact is mandatory for every enrollment or just constrained to be unique when it exists.

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in. The grade is one of A, B, C, D, or F. A student gets at most one grade per offering.

ambiguities.description: It is not explicitly stated whether an Instructor's teaching of multiple offerings 'in the same semester' implies any constraint (e.g., a cap on number of offerings) or is just an illustrative example with no formal rule.
